newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Clear disputes Telecom charges.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Clear disputes Telecom charges.

text.p: Clear Communications said late on Thursday it was not concerned that rival Telecom New Zealand was taking it to court over alleged unpaid bills.
"We are content that Telecom has submitted the issues to the courts," said Clear's general manager of corporate communications, Janiene Bayliss.
Telecom said on Thursday it planned to take Clear to court to get payment, claiming Clear already owed it over NZ$1 million in unpaid bills.
It said the two firms signed a commercial agreement a year ago, where Telecom would supply Clear with services allowing it to interconnect its network with Telecom's.
Prices were agreed at the time and set for a five year term. Telecom said it had been supplying the services since then but in February this year Clear had stopped paid the agreed prices.
Clear's Bayliss said the interconnection agreement signed with Telecom in March last year was "unsatisfactory and unprincipled".

She said the agreement imposed charges and peak/off peak time frames on Clear based on Telecom's business rates, even in relation to residential calls. She said the charges bore no relation to Telecom's costs.
"Since then, Telecom has manipulated the pricing structure of the industry to the point where for certain services Clear must pay Telecom more than Telecom's own customers do.
"Clear believes that both Telecom's conduct and the terms of the agreement which facilitated it are anti-competitive and contravene the Commerce Act."

Bayliss said Telecom had refused to discuss the disagreement, leaving Clear with no option but to withhold the disupted amount each month. She said Clear was still paying Telecom around 90 percent of what it was billed.
Clear is owned in equal proportions by British Telecom, MCI Communications Corp, the New Zealand family-owned Todd Corporation and state-owned Television New Zealand.
Telecom is New Zealand's largest company.
